open_obligations: Check that the arithmetic tasks are generated the same way in both papers.
Note different models (ChatGPT versus Qwen2.5-7B/Llama3.1-8B) and agent counts (3 versus 5).
Check whether Du et al.'s majority vote uses the same number of samples as debate.
out.other_title: Multiagent debate beats single agent, reflection and majority vote on arithmetic and GSM8K
out.rationale: Du et al. report multi-agent debate beats majority vote on arithmetic (81.8% vs 69.0%) and GSM8K (85.0% vs 81.0%) with 3 ChatGPT agents and 2 rounds. Choi, Zhu and Li report majority voting performs on par with MAD in most cases on benchmarks including Arithmetics and GSM8K with 5 Qwen2.5 or Llama3.1 agents, concluding MAD's gains come mostly from ensembling.
out.scope: proposed CHALLENGES: whether multi-agent debate beats majority voting over the same agents on arithmetic and GSM8K

text: The paper reports that MAD does not reliably surpass the simpler majority-voting strategy, which in most cases performs on par with MAD; with the larger Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct, overall MAD performance improves but majority voting still accounts for most of the gains. The authors conclude that MAD's effectiveness is largely driven by ensembling rather than iterative debate.
title: Majority voting performs on par with multi-agent debate across benchmarks
